hypotheses.title: Narrowing-chain joins (ternary / || / &&) re-walk both chains to nil in mergeChains->commonAncestor->chainDepth: O(N^2) in nested conditional depth
hypotheses.issue: mergeChains (called at every ternary, ||/&& and if/else join) calls commonAncestor, which calls chainDepth on both binding chains, walking to nil each time; plus accumPrefix and 3 maps per merge. Nested ternaries / long || chains are O(N^2) in stage 5 (or N=8000: Analysis 1.7s, N=16000: 12.8s).

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Nested conditional / short-circuit chains.

  ternary: return x == 0 ? 0 : x == 1 ? 1 : ... : -1;
  or:      return x == 0 || x == 1 || ... ;

Each nesting level narrows x (x != i) on the false/else path, so the binding chain
seen by level i is i entries deep. Every level then calls
semantics/internal/types/type_resolver_narrowing.go:mergeChains ->
commonAncestor -> chainDepth(c1)+chainDepth(c2), which re-walks both chains
all the way to nil -> O(N^2) total.
Usage: gen_chain.py {ternary|or} N > out.bal
"""
import sys
mode, n = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
if mode == "ternary":
    body = "    return " + "".join(f"x == {i} ? {i} : " for i in range(n)) + "-1;"
    ret = "int"
    check = "if f(3) != 3"
else:
    body = "    return " + " || ".join(f"x == {i}" for i in range(n)) + ";"
    ret = "boolean"
    check = "if !f(3)"
print(f"function f(int x) returns {ret} {{\n{body}\n}}\n\npublic function main() {{\n    {check} {{\n        panic error(\"bad\");\n    }}\n}}")
reproducer.command: python3 gen_chain.py or 8000 > or_8000.bal && go run ./cli/cmd run --stats or_8000.bal

hypotheses.reason: Duplicate of an earlier report ('Narrowing-chain walks make stage-5 type resolution O(N^2) ...'), whose proposed fix (caching chain depth per binding) already covers chainDepth/commonAncestor/mergeChains. Still unfixed on main; the ternary/|| reproducer is an additional data point for that report.

hypotheses.title: Desugaring record-field defaults takes the global function-signature store write lock twice per field, serialising concurrently desugaring modules
hypotheses.issue: desugar/desugar.go:desugarRecordTypeDesc calls setRecordDefaultFnSignature for every record field that has a default value. That calls CompilerContext.AllocateFunctionSignature(nil,false) and AssociateFunctionSignature, which land in context/internal/functionsignatures/store.go (*Store).Allocate and (*Store).Associate. Both take the write lock of a single sync.RWMutex shared by the whole CompilerEnvironment (all modules plus the lang libs). Each call allocates a brand-new, identical empty signature (no params, no rest) and appends it to the global signatures slice, so slice growth and copying happen under the write lock. It also inserts into the global associated map. Stages 5-9 run concurrently per module, and every module's DesugarPackage starts with desugarTopLevelTypeDescs, so all modules hit this lock at the same moment with almost no work in between, and the lock convoys. Mutex profile on the reproducer: ~19.7 s total mutex delay, 98% of it under setRecordDefaultFnSignature (Allocate 12.5 s, Associate 6.8 s). On corpus/bench/10-bench/default-heavy-project-v this is the second-largest contention source (about 18 s mutex delay), after symbolSpacesMu. Effect: the same total work desugars no faster across 16 modules on 4 cores than as one module. Per-module desugar time grows from ~20 ms alone to ~1-1.4 s when run concurrently.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a multi-module Ballerina package: M independent modules, each with
K closed records of F fields that all have default values (desugar creates one
default-value function + function signature per field)."""
import os, sys, shutil
out, M, K, F = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(out)
open(f"{out}/Ballerina.toml", "w").write('[package]\norg = "bench"\nname = "recdefaults"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n')
main = []
for m in range(M):
    d = f"{out}/modules/m{m}"; os.makedirs(d)
    src = [f"public final int seed{m} = {m};\n"]
    for k in range(K):
        src.append(f"public type R{k} record {{|\n")
        for f in range(F):
            src.append(f"    int f{f} = seed{m} + {f};\n" if f % 2 == 0 else f'    string s{f} = "v{f}";\n')
        src.append("|};\n")
    src.append(f"public function make() returns int {{\n    R0 r = {{}};\n    return r.f0;\n}}\n")
    open(f"{d}/m{m}.bal", "w").write("".join(src))
    main.append(f"import recdefaults.m{m};\n")
main.append("\npublic function main() {\n    int s = 0;\n")
for m in range(M):
    main.append(f"    s += m{m}:make();\n")
main.append('    if s == -1 { panic error("x"); }\n}\n')
open(f"{out}/main.bal", "w").write("".join(main))

hypotheses.fix_approach: The prototype pre-allocates one shared empty UntypedFunctionSignature in slot 0 of the store (constant emptyRef = 1, set in NewStore). It adds Store.AssociateEmpty(syms []SymbolRef), exposed as CompilerEnvironment/CompilerContext.AssociateEmptyFunctionSignature, which links a whole batch of symbols to that ref under one lock acquisition and keeps Associate's 'already associated with a different ref -> false' rule. desugarRecordTypeDesc collects the default-function refs while looping over the fields and associates them once per record. That removes the per-field allocation and replaces 2 write-lock acquisitions per field with 1 per record. SetFunctionTypedSignature is still called per field. Sharing is safe because every reader takes the signature by value (Get/GetByRef/Ref, walkCallArgs, the symbolpool serializer, which already dedups by ref, and the ls fingerprint). UpdateIncludedRecords only runs on function-declaration refs in stages 4-5, and a zero-param signature has nothing to update. Signature ref numbers shift by one; nothing depends on absolute values. Rejected alternative: a lock-free store (sync.Map / atomic chunks). It cut the concurrent case further but slowed the single-module case to ~1.5 s desugar because of per-operation overhead. Remaining contention on many-module packages is mostly the known symbolSpacesMu RWMutex. Verified with make test and make test-race (both pass).

notes: Explorers also re-observed several already-reported issues still present on main: isLaxInner/IsSameType(json) on self.x access in large classes (~cubic, 30.7 s at 4000 methods), propagatedRecordFieldAnnotations on alias chains, lookupBindingInner with many workers, and symbolSpacesMu (context/env.go) as the largest lock on multi-module packages.
